headline: SpaceX thrives. Blue Origin clears. Viasat scores.
deck: This week saw SpaceX's continued dominance, Blue Origin's recovery, and a hefty military contract for Viasat and SES.

stories.head: Space Force hands $437M to Viasat and SES
stories.body: The Space Force awarded a $437 million contract to Viasat and SES for four military satellites, a move that underscores the growing demand for geostationary capabilities. This contract comes amidst increasing geopolitical tensions, as the military seeks to bolster its satellite infrastructure. With this deal, Viasat and SES are set to enhance their positions in the defense sector.
stories.soWhat: In a world where space is now a contested domain, the ability to secure contracts like this could make or break companies in the coming years.

stories.head: SpaceX launches its first Starship V3—successfully
stories.body: SpaceX successfully launched its first Starship V3, achieving most of its test objectives and reinforcing its status as the go-to player in the launch market. This comes after a series of setbacks with previous iterations, showcasing SpaceX's resilience and engineering prowess. The rapid iterations are a testament to their operational efficiency, as they continue to push the envelope.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX can keep this momentum, it will be difficult for competitors to catch up, especially with their established launch cadence.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M; co-orbital security focus
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C round, reaching a valuation of $1.6 billion, with a clear focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. This funding reflects the increasing interest from the DoD in private solutions for national security challenges in space. As defense budgets tighten, companies that can demonstrate tangible results will likely attract more attention.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that co-orbital capabilities will be the next big thing in defense, but execution will be key.

watchlist.title: NASA's reorganization implications for contractors
watchlist.body: As NASA shuffles its internal structure, contractors should prepare for potential shifts in priorities and funding.

watchlist.title: Blue Origin's next steps post-investigation
watchlist.body: With the investigation behind them, Blue Origin's next launch will be crucial for regaining trust in their capabilities.

watchlist.title: Impacts of hypersonic test delays
watchlist.body: The continued delays in hypersonic testing could hinder the U.S. military's strategic edge, raising questions about funding allocations.

watchlist.title: Upcoming Space Force budget discussions
watchlist.body: As the FY27 budget discussions heat up, watch for shifts in funding priorities that could affect multiple contractors.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
